authors: Wang, D., Shelhamer, E., Liu, S., Olshausen, B. & Darrell, T.
title: Tent: Fully test-time adaptation by entropy minimization
relevance: The method STATE's open item 3 is implicitly proposing - re-estimate BN statistics on the target year and minimize prediction entropy, no labels and no source data needed. Read the objective carefully before adopting it: entropy minimization optimizes for CONFIDENCE, and our documented failure mode is near-threshold misses (2013: 91% of missed forest sits between prob 0.12 and threshold). Pushing those pixels away from the decision boundary hardens the existing bias rather than correcting it - inference-time confirmation bias, the same mechanism as Arazo 2020 (ID 89).

title: Towards stable test-time adaptation in dynamic wild world
relevance: Documents when test-time adaptation fails outright or actively HARMS the model: mixed distribution shifts, small batch sizes, and online imbalanced label distribution. All three describe our deployment exactly - three sensors plus contractor changes, an inference batch of 32 on Colab, and canopy that is spatially clustered so a batch can be pure forest or pure water. Its fix (drop high-gradient noisy samples, seek a flat minimum) is the minimum safe configuration if we try TTA at all; without it this is a plausible way to make several years quietly worse with no label to catch it.

authors: Wang, Q., Fink, O., Van Gool, L. & Dai, D.
title: Continual test-time domain adaptation
relevance: Adapts across a SEQUENCE of shifting domains rather than one target, and addresses the error accumulation and catastrophic forgetting that arise when adaptation is applied repeatedly - which is the shape of our problem if we adapt year by year across 18 acquisitions in temporal order. Directly relevant to whether per-year adaptation drifts cumulatively, which would corrupt exactly the temporal signal our per-crown validity intervals depend on. Argues for resetting to source weights periodically rather than chaining adaptations, a design choice we would otherwise get wrong by default.

authors: Wang, P., Yao, W., Shao, J. & He, Z.
title: Test-time adaptation for geospatial point cloud semantic segmentation with distinct domain shifts
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 229, 422-435
relevance: The peer-reviewed geospatial benchmark of the methods above - AdaBN, TENT, DIGA and ROID compared across five datasets under shifts in location, platform, modality and TIME, the same axes we span. Gives us realistic expected gains for TTA on geospatial data rather than the ImageNet-corruption numbers the method papers report, so we can decide whether the effect size justifies the risk Niu 2023 documents. Caveat for transfer: it is point-cloud, not aerial imagery, so treat the ranking as indicative and the magnitudes as unverified for our modality.
